header:
Date: 2026-09-15
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Sara Kim (Redwood AE), Miguel Ortega (Redwood SE), Leah Park (Redwood CSM), Priya Nair (BlueWave Head of MLOps), Daniel Cho (BlueWave Platform), Amira Farid (BlueWave Compliance), Marcus Li (BlueWave SRE)
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on Dedicated sizing and the surge/runbook for an upcoming pilot. Reviewed results from initial warm-up tests, discussed autoscale policy parameters (min/max, ramp, pre-warm), burst capacity options and billing implications, and compliance concerns around audit logs and KMS. Agreed on a 1-hour burst simulation run by Redwood SE and follow-up SOC2/KMS walkthrough.
topics: Compliance: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, retention
transcript:
[00:00] Sara Kim: okay everyone thanks for joining, we're gonna run 45 minutes, quick agenda is dedicated sizing, runbook review for the pilot surge, and then next steps. Priya, you wanna kick with what changed since last week?
[00:12] Priya Nair: yeah thanks Sara. Uh we've got a refined traffic trace from the staging gateway, the p95 is about 2.1k tok/s and p99 spikes to 7.4k for short bursts, also saw a 30s spike pattern tied to batch jobs. We want to validate the burst plan doesn't blow the budget.
[00:28] Miguel Ortega: mm-hmm, got it. Did you attach the trace? I pulled the csv but there's some tokenization mapping differences - looks like token counts are slightly higher because of the tokenizer mismatch.
[00:37] Daniel Cho: right that was my bad, I used the upstream tokenizer in staging which adds ~8% tokens. We'll normalize and re-upload.
[00:45] Sara Kim: cool. So today's focus — runbook walk-through. I put a draft at link: https://redwood.runbooks/bluewave-burst-playbook-v2.pdf and also small spreadsheet with sizing. Anyone not have access?
[00:58] Marcus Li: I have access. Quick Q: the min pool size in the doc is 2x A40, is that still the recommendation?
[01:07] Miguel Ortega: yeah for your workloads the baseline min is 2 A40s to keep latency stable for regular traffic. For burst we recommend a burst pool of up to 8 GPUs with a pre-warm window. The autoscale policy we propose is min:2, target_util: 65%, max:8, cooldown: 90s, ramp: 60s. That gives room for short spikes without cold starts.
[01:30] Priya Nair: when you say pre-warm window — do you mean we pre-allocate GPUs before traffic or we just pin weight to a warm cache?
[01:37] Miguel Ortega: both options. Pre-warm means spin up instances ahead of an expected surge (we'll do a timezone-based scheduling or webhook to trigger). We also use prefix/KV cache — keep hot KV shards resident so the decoder warm hits and reduces initial latency. Note: long sequences may still require KV builds.
[01:55] Daniel Cho: there was one test where the KV cache was recorded as K V cask in the logs, so the auto-detection didn't flag cache hits properly. Could be a naming mismatch in the metric tags.
[02:06] Miguel Ortega: yeah that's a tagging issue, we'll push a fix to the metric exporter.
[02:10] Leah Park: from the CSM side we want to make sure the runbook has clear rollback steps — what to do if p99 exceeds SLO for 3 consecutive minutes.
[02:21] Sara Kim: good call. Runbook section 4.2 covers fallback: route to smaller model variant or degrade to single-turn compressive mode and enable early-stop to trim tokens. We'll add explicit thresholds and an on-call alert play.
[02:36] Amira Farid: on the compliance side, I'm worried about burst logs. During a burst, we generate lots of request traces — what's retained, who can access, and are they encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys?
[02:48] Miguel Ortega: yes — Dedicated supports KMS. We can configure customer-managed keys and have audit logs forwarded to your SIEM via an S3 sink. Retention is configurable; by default we keep 90 days in the platform but can export to long-term archive.
[03:02] Amira Farid: do you support HSM-backed keys?
[03:06] Miguel Ortega: yes, HSM/KMS via the cloud provider is supported in the Private deployment; for Dedicated we integrate with your KMS—if you require HSM we can validate with infra. We'll put a compliance checklist in the runbook.
[03:18] Sara Kim: note — action item to schedule SOC2 + KMS walkthrough with Amira.
[03:22] Priya Nair: another question — billing during burst: is it per-minute allocated GPU, or do you bill per-second for the extra capacity? We need clear line for forecasting.
[03:32] Sara Kim: good question. For Dedicated base reservation we bill monthly committed. Burst usage is billed hourly for added capacity in the addendum — we're proposing a per-minute metered model in the spreadsheet to match your usage shape. I'll send a version with a minute granularity example.
[03:49] Daniel Cho: hmm, need to model worst-case — 10k tok/s sustained for 1 hour, what would that look like?
[03:57] Miguel Ortega: rough calc — with our current profiling a A40 at 4-bit quant gives ~1.2k tok/s for your model at 512 seq with continuous batching. So to hit 10k you'd need about 9 GPUs; we recommend 10 for headroom. We'll run the sim to confirm.
[04:14] Priya Nair: what about batching effects? If we tune batch size larger we might get cost savings but risk tail latency.
[04:21] Miguel Ortega: exactly. Batching reduces tokens-per-second cost but increases p99 unless the request patterns align. Our policy suggestion: dynamic batching with max_batch=64 and per-model latency SLO override — keep max_latency 250ms. For critical routes you can pin small batch sizes.
[04:37] Marcus Li: I'd like to see the p99 vs batch-size curve from the lab tests.
[04:41] Miguel Ortega: I'll attach the benchmark plots from yesterday — link to s3: s3://redwood-bench/bluewave/bench-2026-09-14.png. There was a small transcription glitch in the test logs where "quantize" came out as "can ties" in the exporter. Ignore that field.
[04:57] Sara Kim: the runbook also suggests a canary for the burst add: start with 20% traffic to burst pool, monitor errors and latency for 30m, then increment 50% then 100%. Any objections?
[05:09] Daniel Cho: sounds fine. How do we route requests for canary? Path-based? Token-level?
[05:15] Miguel Ortega: we recommend header-based routing at the gateway so you can flip easily. Also have a fallback route to hosted Redwood model in case Dedicated saturates — configured in policy chain.
[05:27] Priya Nair: what about fallback model quality? The hosted model is a different checkpoint and we need to avoid hallucinations for certain clinical prompts.
[05:36] Sara Kim: put that in the risk section — we'll run an eval set of clinical prompts as a pre-flight. If fallback quality is unacceptable, we will disable auto-fallback and only do manual failover.
[05:48] Amira Farid: on audit retention again — what about PII redaction in logs? During debugging we sometimes see PHI tokens in traces. Can Redwood redact before storing?
[05:58] Miguel Ortega: we have a post-processing hook — you can enable automated redaction filters that mask PHI patterns before logs hit S3. We'll include recommended regex and examples in the runbook.
[06:10] Marcus Li: ok good. Back to capacity — is there support for burst across regions? If east coast saturates can we spill to europe pool?
[06:20] Miguel Ortega: cross-region spill is supported but with higher latency. We advise local region first, then cross-region as last result; you'll need data residency guardrails. Also billing and egress considerations.
[06:30] Priya Nair: bluewave has a 0.5% allowed cross-region requests for privacy -- we need that enforced.
[06:36] Sara Kim: add to runbook: cross-region spill disabled by default; require explicit flag per deployment.
[06:41] Daniel Cho: anything about kernel selection and quantization? We saw weird perf differences between int8 and 4-bit quant.
[06:49] Miguel Ortega: right — kernel selection is auto but for your model the 4-bit path is generally best cost/perf. There are some sequences where int8 wins for tail latency on longer contexts. We'll include a recommendation matrix per sequence length.
[07:03] Priya Nair: can we pin kernel selection for a deployment?
[07:06] Miguel Ortega: yes we can force kernel profiles in the model config. We'll add that to the runbook.
[07:10] Leah Park: users often want an escalation path during the pilot — add Redwoods on-call and SRE contacts and hours.
[07:17] Sara Kim: done. Section 6 lists 24/7 on-call and 12-hr daytime ops contact.
[07:22] Marcus Li: I want to call out warmup cost — if we pre-warm 8 GPUs for every expected surge window, that's a lot of standing cost. Can we pre-warm the model binary but not fully allocate GPU memory until traffic arrives?
[07:36] Miguel Ortega: there is a partial pre-warm option — keep a lightweight container with model weights on disk and then do a rapid load into memory on trigger; reduces full allocation time but still has a cold-start delta. For very short spikes we'd rely on KV cache and a small burst headroom.
[07:52] Priya Nair: interesting. For our 30s spikes that might be the sweet spot.
[07:56] Daniel Cho: ok what about the telemetry during the burst run — we need per-token breakdowns, tail latency, CPU/GPU temp, queue depth.
[08:05] Miguel Ortega: the dashboard includes token-level cost and queue depth; we can add a high-frequency trace for the simulation run and export csv.
[08:12] Sara Kim: recap of decisions: Redwood will run the 1h burst sim, attach metrics & plots; BlueWave to normalize traffic trace and confirm allowed cross-region percent; Redwood to update runbook with explicit rollback thresholds, canary steps, KMS/HSM checklist, redaction regex, and updated pricing.
[08:29] Priya Nair: yep, and please call out worst-case cost example in the pricing spreadsheet.
[08:34] Sara Kim: will do. Any other Qs?
[08:36] Amira Farid: just one — data in-flight encryption for cross-region spill?
[08:40] Miguel Ortega: TLS 1.3 yes, and you can enforce mTLS between your gateway and our endpoints. We'll include sample cert rotation steps.
[08:49] Daniel Cho: that's it from infra.
[08:51] Leah Park: next sync same time next week?
[08:54] Sara Kim: yes same time. I'll create calendar invite after we update the runbook.
[08:58] Priya Nair: thanks all.
[09:00] Sara Kim: thanks, meeting adjourned.

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-words (e.g., "K V cask" for KV cache, "can ties" for quantize).
